items.headline: Backfill: sand and cement supplier penalised $135,000 in the Industrial Court after a truck crane struck overhead powerlines
items.summary: SafeWork NSW announced on 21 August that Kens Sand & Cement Pty Ltd was fined $135,000 in the Industrial Court of NSW after pleading guilty to a category 2 style breach of its primary duty to workers under the Work Health and Safety Act. The incident dates to February 2023, when a worker unloading a bag of sand at a Dundas construction site brought the truck-mounted crane into contact with a live low-voltage overhead powerline, pulling it down and damaging the truck cab; nobody was hurt. The regulator's commissioner framed the case around the point that exclusion-distance controls for mobile plant near overhead lines are long settled and well documented. This item is logged now because it was missed when published and the 25 August digest incorrectly recorded the 19 August Fitzmoore penalty as SafeWork's most recent release.
items.so_what: Low direct claims significance, since no worker was injured and no compensation liability followed, but it is a useful marker of what the NSW regulator is still prosecuting to conviction three and a half years after the event, and of the penalty range now attaching to a guilty plea on a well-known physical control failure with a near-miss outcome. For underwriters, the more practical read is the enforcement tail: exposure on a construction or transport risk can crystallise as a court outcome years after the incident and long after the policy period in which it occurred. It also sits against SafeWork's stated priority list of falls, psychosocial harm, hazardous substances and plant, confirming that plant enforcement has not been displaced by the psychosocial push.
